title: I Applied the Curling-Club Ice-Sheet Clock to the Skip Who Took Our Hammer

parts.text: I stepped on sheet three at 6:02 p.m. and skip Marla was already throwing our numbered hammer. The board said: ONE SHEET. TWO HOURS. HAMMER STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-four, league lead, holding a clipboard that listed our ice. Marla shrugged. "Skips are the sheet." I photographed the board, the booking, and her stone on our hog line. Then I asked for the ice log. At 6:11 the ice tech pinged why Marla's name was on our hammer. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The ice tech can see Marla's hammer on sheet three during our booking.

social.video_title: She threw our numbered hammer on our ice — Part 1/2
social.description: Curling sheet, a skip on our hog line, a two-hour clock she posted. I logged the throw. Would you have asked for the ice log?

parts.text: Marla called it warm-up until the ice tech asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the hog-line still. The hammer went back to our handle. Marla ran her own two hours and told the next skip atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word skips use when a booking exists. Sheet policy now has a second line: SKIPS ARE NOT THE ICE. I keep our hammer on a labeled hook. Marla brown-bags her jokes. The sheet finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Skips are not the ice — Part 2/2
social.description: Ice log, numbered hammer, and a second line on the board. Was warm-up ever our hog line?
